subtitle: Upon an Ancient Pillar, a New King Writes His Name

panels.shot: low-angle wide of an ancient iron pillar rising against the Delhi sky, Vigraharaja IV in the foreground touching it with one hand
panels.action: Vigraharaja IV stands in armour beside an ancient pillar in Delhi, one hand resting on the dark metal as his scribes kneel nearby, the city’s walls and the Yamuna haze stretching behind him.

dialogue.text: In the twelfth century, Vigraharaja IV seized Delhi from the Tomaras—and carved his triumph onto an older emperor’s pillar, hoping Ashoka’s iron would remember his name.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी में विग्रहराज चौथे ने तोमारों से दिल्ली छीनी, और अशोक के पुराने लौह स्तंभ पर अपनी जीत खुदवा दी—कि लोहा उसका नाम याद रखे।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over north India between the Aravallis and the Yamuna
panels.action: A parchment-map style view shows the Aravalli hills, the Yamuna river, Delhi, Hansi, Chittor and Naddula marked with tiny fort icons under a hazy monsoon sky.

dialogue.text: Around 1150 CE, the land of Sapadalaksha stretched between the Aravallis and the Yamuna—border country where Chahamanas, Tomaras, Chaulukyas and Ghaznavids tested each other’s strength.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1150 ईस्वी में सपादलक्ष देश अरावली से यमुना तक फैला था—सीमांत धरती, जहाँ चाहमाना, तोमरा, चालुक्य और ग़ज़नवी एक-दूसरे की ताकत आज़माते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot in a palace hall, slightly low angle
panels.action: Young Vigraharaja IV in royal robes listens intently in a stone-pillared hall, a court scholar reading from a palm-leaf manuscript while a map of frontier forts lies unrolled before them.

dialogue.text: Vigraharaja, grandson of the warrior Arnoraja, inherited not peace but unfinished wars—Tomara Delhi on one side, Chaulukya power from Gujarat on another, and Turushka raids skirting his borders.

i18n.hi: योद्धा अर्णोराज का पोता विग्रहराज विरासत में शांति नहीं, अधूरी जंगें पाता है—एक ओर तोमरा की दिल्ली, दूसरी ओर गुजरात से चालुक्य ताकत, और किनारों पर टूट पड़ते तुरुष्क हमले।

panels.shot: close-up on Vigraharaja’s face, thoughtful, lit by lamplight
panels.action: Vigraharaja IV leans over a detailed map, lamplight catching the sharp lines of his face as his fingers rest on the mark of Delhi, his brow furrowed in calculation.

dialogue.speaker: vigraharaja_iv
dialogue.text: Delhi guards the road and the river. Without it, Sapadalaksha is a house without a door.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली सड़क और नदी दोनों की रखवाली है। उसके बिना सपादलक्ष बिना दरवाज़े का घर है।

panels.shot: wide battlefield shot from behind Vigraharaja on horseback
panels.action: Armoured Vigraharaja IV on horseback overlooks his cavalry and infantry forming up on dusty plains facing the distant low silhouette of Delhi’s walls and towers.

dialogue.text: The Bijolia inscription would later say simply that he ‘took Delhi and Hansi from the Tomaras.’ The stone spares us the dust, the marches and the bargaining that came before those words.

i18n.hi: बीजौलिया शिलालेख बस इतना कहेगा कि उसने ‘दिल्ली और हांसी तोमारों से ली।’ पत्थर हमें नहीं दिखाता वह धूल, वे लामबंदियाँ और सौदे, जिनसे पहले ये शब्द गढ़े गए।

panels.shot: medium shot at a city gate, eye-level
panels.action: At Delhi’s main gate, Vigraharaja IV sits upright on his horse as Tomara nobles approach on foot, heads bowed, offering keys on a platter against the backdrop of solid stone walls.

dialogue.text: Delhi did not vanish with one charge. Its Tomara lords bent instead of breaking, yielding their fort to him and remaining as vassals under the Chahamana banner.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली एक धावे में नहीं मिटती। उसके तोमरा स्वामी टूटने की बजाय झुक जाते हैं—किला उसे सौंप कर चाहमाना झंडे के नीचे उसके सामंत बनते हैं।

panels.shot: interior wide in Delhi palace audience hall
panels.action: In a newly-claimed Delhi hall, Vigraharaja IV sits on a low throne, Tomara chiefs kneeling at a respectful distance as envoys bearing Ghaznavid-style caps and Chaulukya dress are shown kept waiting.

dialogue.text: From Delhi and Hansi, he watched two worlds: westward the Ghaznavid and Ghurid frontier, south-west the Chaulukyas of Gujarat. The city became his listening post on empire.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली और हांसी से वह दो दुनिया देखता है—पश्चिम में ग़ज़नवी-ग़ुरी सरहद, दक्षिण-पश्चिम में गुजरात के चालुक्य। शहर उसका सम्राज्य-सुनने वाला चौकीघर बन जाता है।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-action shot near a fort, slightly low angle
panels.action: On rocky ground near a hillfort, Vigraharaja IV raises his sword in command while his troops advance, the crenellated walls of Hansi looming ahead, siege ladders and shielded archers frozen mid-move.

dialogue.text: Hansi, another Tomara stronghold, fell in the same arc of campaigns. Control of both Delhi and Hansi tightened his grip on the northern routes and gave his armies depth.

i18n.hi: हांसी, तोमरों का एक और गढ़, इन्हीं अभियानों की लहर में गिरता है। दिल्ली और हांसी दोनों पर पकड़ से उसकी मुट्ठी उत्तर की राहों पर कस जाती है और सेनाएँ गहरी हो जाती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a meeting of commanders in a tent
panels.action: Inside a war tent, Vigraharaja IV stands over a map marked with Chittor and Naddula as commanders point and discuss, a sword and helmet resting beside the chart.

dialogue.text: But his ambition did not stop at Delhi. To the south-west, Chittor and Naddula were held by men loyal to Kumarapala’s Chaulukya power and to collateral Chahamana lines that tested his authority.

i18n.hi: लेकिन उसकी चाहत दिल्ली पर नहीं रुकती। दक्षिण-पश्चिम में चित्तौड़ और नद्दुला पर कुमारपाल के चालुक्य समर्थक और सगोत्र चाहमाना बैठे हैं, जो उसकी सत्ता को चुनौती देते हैं।

panels.shot: battlefield wide with fortress in background, dusk light
panels.action: At dusk before the steep hill of Chittor, Vigraharaja IV’s army forms in lines, siege engines in the rear, as the fortress rises above rocky cliffs under a darkening sky.

dialogue.text: The Bijolia rock inscription, carved near a Jain temple in 1170, recalls how he met the Chaulukya governor Sajjana at Chittor—and killed him, avenging his father’s defeat.

i18n.hi: 1170 के आसपास जैन मंदिर के पास कटे बीजौलिया शिलालेख में लिखा है कि वह चित्तौड़ में चालुक्य सुबेदार सज्जन से भिड़ा—और उसे मार गिराया, पिता की हार का बदला लेते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up of Vigraharaja mid-stride inside Chittor, triumphant yet grim
panels.action: Within Chittor’s stone streets, Vigraharaja IV walks forward, helmet in hand, his face set and reflective as soldiers secure the gate towers behind him.

dialogue.speaker: vigraharaja_iv
dialogue.text: My father’s humiliation lies buried here. Let our record be different.

i18n.hi: मेरे पिता की बेइज़्ज़ती यहीं दफ्न है। हमारी कहानी अलग लिखी जाएगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vigraharaja confronting Naddula chiefs
panels.action: In a courtyard at Naddula, Vigraharaja IV stands firm while armed local chiefs, the Naddula Chahamanas, stand tense but subdued as his banner flies over their smaller flags.

dialogue.text: He pressed onward to Naddula, suppressing that branch of his own house, folding their lands into his. Sapadalaksha was being remade as a single, firmer spine.

i18n.hi: वह नद्दुला की ओर बढ़ता है, अपने ही कुल की उस शाखा को दबाकर उनकी ज़मीन अपने में मिला लेता है। सपादलक्ष एक नई, सख़्त रीढ़ की तरह गढ़ा जा रहा था।

panels.shot: action wide of frontier skirmish, semi-long
panels.action: On an open plain, Chahamana cavalry confronts a smaller force with Central Asian style helmets and mail; lances are levelled, but the scene freezes at the moment of tense standoff rather than clash.

dialogue.text: On his north-western edge he pushed back Ghaznavid and other Turushka pressure. Later panegyrics would call him a ‘conqueror of Muslims,’ but the frontier then was power and plunder, not crusade.

i18n.hi: उत्तर-पश्चिम किनारे पर वह ग़ज़नवी और दूसरे तुरुष्क दबावों को धकेलता है। बाद के गुणगान उसे ‘मु슬मान-विजेता’ कहेंगे, पर उस समय सरहद धर्मयुद्ध नहीं, ताकत और लूट का میدان थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Delhi pillar being moved on rollers, side view
panels.action: Workers strain with ropes and wooden rollers to move a massive inscribed pillar across the ground near Delhi, while Vigraharaja IV watches from horseback, pointing to a new foundation site.

dialogue.text: Near Delhi stood an older voice in iron: a pillar bearing Ashoka’s edicts, brought from Topra. Under Vigraharaja, it was set up anew, given a fresh message in an ancient body.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली के पास लोहे में जड़ा एक पुराना बोलता स्वर खड़ा था—अशोक के फ़रमान वाला स्तंभ, जो तोप्रा से लाया गया था। विग्रहराज के अधीन इसे फिर खड़ा किया गया, प्राचीन देह में नया संदेश भरकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vigraharaja and a scribe beside the pillar
panels.action: At the base of the re-erected pillar, Vigraharaja IV stands with a court scribe who kneels, stylus poised over a prepared stone slab, while the king gestures to a text draft on a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: On that pillar and in the Delhi-Shivalik inscription of 1164, he claimed rule ‘between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas’—a boast, but also a map of how far his reach had grown.

i18n.hi: उसी स्तंभ पर और 1164 के दिल्ली-शिवालिक शिलालेख में वह दावा करता है कि उसकी हुकूमत ‘हिमालय से विंध्य’ तक है—अति-शेखी, पर यह भी नक्शा है कि उसकी पहुंच कहाँ तक फैल चुकी थी।

panels.shot: close-up of chisel biting into stone, low angle with Vigraharaja blurred behind
panels.action: A mason’s hand drives a chisel into stone at the pillar’s base, carving clear Nagari letters, while Vigraharaja IV’s figure stands slightly out of focus behind, arms folded.

dialogue.text: The Chahamana habit of inscription reached new confidence: this king wrote his victories into rock and iron, anchoring his story beside Ashoka’s, trusting that script would outlast song.

i18n.hi: चाहमाना शिलालेख की आदत अब नए भरोसे से भर जाती है—यह राजा अपनी जीत पत्थर और लोहे में लिखवाता है, अपनी कथा को अशोक के साथ गाड़ देता है, जैसे मानता हो कि लेखन गीत से लंबा जीएगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Bijolia cliff with inscription, slight upward angle
panels.action: On a rocky outcrop near a Jain temple at Bijolia, artisans perch on scaffolding chiselling lines into the cliff as Vigraharaja IV visits on horseback, gazing up at the growing inscription panel.

dialogue.text: At Bijolia, near a Jain temple, his poet Gunabhadra carved a long rock inscription in 1170. It told of Delhi, Hansi and Chittor, and set his genealogy in stone as if to fix his line in time.

i18n.hi: बीजौलिया में, जैन मंदिर के पास, उसके कवि गुणभद्र ने 1170 में एक लंबा शिलालेख तराशा। उसमें दिल्ली, हांसी, चित्तौड़ की कथाएँ थीं, और उसकी वंशावली पत्थर पर ऐसे जड़ी जैसे वक़्त में उसकी रेखा को जाम दिया जाए।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot, Vigraharaja alone near the pillar at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Vigraharaja IV stands alone at the base of the Delhi pillar, one hand lightly touching its cool surface as the sky darkens and the city’s silhouette glows faintly in the distance.

dialogue.speaker: vigraharaja_iv
dialogue.text: Ashoka wrote of dharma; I write of battles. Yet both of us fear forgetting.

i18n.hi: अशोक ने धर्म लिखा, मैं युद्ध लिखता हूँ। फिर भी हम दोनों को भूल जाने का डर है।

panels.shot: long shot of the pillar centuries later with modern skyline faintly suggested
panels.action: The ancient pillar stands tall in an open court as the light changes, with layered silhouettes of later walls and domes behind it, hinting at centuries passing.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Ashoka’s edicts and Vigraharaja’s boasts still share the same iron and stone. His conquests faded, but his choice to write on old monuments reminds us how every age tries to borrow eternity.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीत गईं, पर अशोक के फ़रमान और विग्रहराज की शेखी आज भी उसी लोहे और पत्थर पर साथ खड़े हैं। उसकी फतहें मिट गईं, पर पुराने स्मारकों पर लिखने की उसकी ज़िद दिखाती है कि हर युग अमरता उधार लेना चाहता है।

title_i18n.en: Vigraharaja Wins Delhi and the Pillar Edict
title_i18n.hi: विग्रहराज ने जीती दिल्ली, लौह स्तंभ पर नया फ़रमान

subtitle_i18n.en: Upon an Ancient Pillar, a New King Writes His Name
subtitle_i18n.hi: प्राचीन स्तंभ पर, नया राजा लिखता अपना नाम
